# Complete Architectural Analysis of the Rogue Wave Codebase

## Problem statement

The Rogue Wave project (a Unity 2022.3 first-person roguelike wave shooter) has grown organically to ~27.4k lines of first-party C# across 214 files with no architecture documentation. New contributors (human and AI agents) must reverse-engineer the codebase from scratch to understand how the game systems (roguelite progression, procedural level generation, AI director, narrative, stats, save system) fit together. There is no `docs/` directory today.

## Users

- **Developers (human and AI agents)** working on the Rogue Wave codebase — the primary beneficiaries. Example user story: "As a developer new to the project, I want a single architectural reference document so that I can find the system responsible for a feature and understand how it interacts with other systems within minutes rather than hours."
- **Project maintainer (TheWizardsCode)** — needs an accurate, up-to-date map of the codebase to guide refactoring (e.g., the noted god-class `RogueWaveGameMode`), onboarding, and future work (e.g., Unity upgrade).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A comprehensive architecture document is created at `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (repo root) describing the full architecture of the Rogue Wave codebase.
- [ ] The document covers all first-party code: `Assets/_Rogue Wave` (Runtime + Editor), `Assets/Wizards Code/Game State`, `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller`, `Assets/Wizards Code/Command Terminal`, plus the Rogue Wave command assemblies.
- [ ] The document includes: (1) project overview & tech stack, (2) assembly/module dependency map (asmdef), (3) scene/flow diagram of the game loop, (4) per-system analysis of the major subsystems: Roguelite meta-progression (Recipe system, RogueLiteManager/PersistentData/RunData, CampaignManager, NanobotManager), procedural level generation (WFC: LevelGenerator, TileDefinitions, WfcDefinition), AI director & enemy system (AIDirector, BasicEnemyController, Spawner/WaveDefinition), combat/weapons, Game Stats & Achievements, Story Teller (Ink), save/profile system, UI/HUD, dev tools.
- [ ] The document identifies key architectural patterns (data-driven ScriptableObject design, event systems, NeoFPS extension points) and key third-party dependencies with their role (NeoFPS, Ink, Steamworks.NET, Feel, Discord telemetry).
- [ ] The document includes an observations/risks section noting maintainability concerns (e.g., `RogueWaveGameMode` god-class, hard-coded stat keys, duplicated victory coroutines, absence of first-party unit tests and CI).
- [ ] All facts in the document are verified against the actual code (file paths and class names accurate); the analysis is grounded in the repository state at commit `0bf61611` (dev branch).
- [ ] The analysis is recorded as a comment on work item RW-0MS9G83FW00295E5 with the commit hash once delivered.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (documentation only — verify no code changes are introduced; project has no first-party unit tests today).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Technical:** Unity 2022.3.52f1 LTS; URP; C# with asmdefs. Document must reflect actual code — no invented architecture.
- **Repository boundary rules:** The analysis is read-only with respect to `Assets/` source code; the only file created is the documentation file. Do not modify third-party code.
- **Environment:** No Unity editor available in this environment; analysis is performed by static code reading. Git LFS tools are not installed (some binary assets cannot be inspected).
- **Licensing:** Third-party assets (NeoFPS, Feel, etc.) are commercial; only their interfaces/roles should be documented from what is visible in the repo.

## Existing state

- Unity 2022.3.52f1 project, 34 first-party scenes, 940+ commits on `dev`, 8.4 GB Assets (mostly third-party).
- First-party C#: ~27.4k lines / 214 files in `Assets/_Rogue Wave`, `Assets/Wizards Code/Game State`, `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller`, `Assets/Wizards Code/Command Terminal`.
- Architecture is data-driven: game content (recipes, levels, tiles, waves, stats, achievements, scenarios) is authored as ScriptableObjects under `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Resources/` and loaded at runtime.
- Core FPS framework is NeoFPS; the game extends `FpsSoloGameCustomisable`, `FpsSoloPlayerController`, `FpsSoloCharacter`, NeoSceneManager, NeoSerializedGameObject (save), and modular firearms.
- No `docs/` directory, no first-party unit tests, no CI workflows (only GitHub issue templates).

## Desired change

- Create `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — a single, accurate, well-structured architecture reference for the codebase.
- The document should be self-contained (no dependency on being able to open the project in Unity) and stable enough to remain useful while the codebase evolves.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — **NEW** the main deliverable: full architectural analysis.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Game Management/RogueWaveGameMode.cs` — game-mode orchestrator; central to run flow (spawn, victory/death, extraction, loadout, stats).
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Game Management/ScenarioManager.cs` — scenario-driven level loading.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Roguelite/RogueLiteManager.cs` — singleton manager; profiles, save/load, scene names, run/persistent data access.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Roguelite/RogueLitePersistentData.cs` — permanent progression data model.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Roguelite/RogueLiteRunData.cs` — per-run recipes/loadout model.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Roguelite/CampaignManager.cs` — campaign selection/unlocking; extends StoryManager.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Roguelite/Recipe/*` — recipe system (RecipeManager, AbstractRecipe, IRecipe, WeaponRecipe, etc.).
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Nanobots/NanobotManager.cs` — in-run economy/build system.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Levels/LevelGenerator.cs` — WFC level generation core.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Levels/WfcDefinition.cs`, `TileDefinition.cs`, `Levels/Tiles/*` — level/tile definitions.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Enemies/AIDirector.cs` — difficulty/pressure director.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Enemies/BasicEnemyController.cs`, `Spawner.cs` — enemies and spawning.
- `Assets/Wizards Code/Game State/Runtime/Stats/GameStatsManager.cs` — stats, achievements, telemetry (Steam/Discord).
- `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Runtime/StoryManager.cs` — Ink narrative engine.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/UI/*`, `UI/Hud/*` — UI/HUD systems.
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Editor/*` — editor tooling (data windows, validation, voice acting).
- `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/org.wizardscode.roguewave.asmdef` + `Editor/org.wizardscode.roguewave.editor.asmdef` — assembly structure.
- `Packages/manifest.json`, `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`, `.gitmodules`, `README.md` — tech-stack context.

## Related work

- No existing docs in the repository (`docs/` does not exist). The automated find_related report surfaced only agent-framework files (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py`); these are tooling files, not game-project files, and are not genuinely related.
- Related (unrelated scope) work items in the worklog:
  - `Ensure we are up and running (RW-0MS9D47BD002JNPL)` — idea stage; environment sanity check.
  - `Upgarde to the latest Unity version (RW-0MS9D4MJS003O7MO)` — idea stage; Unity upgrade. The architecture doc will be useful context for this.
  - The local AGENTS.md references `docs/dev/release-process.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (for the worklog tooling) — establishing `docs/` as the conventional location for such documents in this repo.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The deliverable lives at `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` in the repo root, following the `docs/` convention referenced by AGENTS.md. If the operator prefers another location this can be changed during review.
- **Assumption:** "Complete architectural analysis" covers first-party game code plus the roles of the third-party frameworks; it does not require documenting every third-party asset.
- **Risk:** Static analysis without a Unity editor may misrepresent runtime wiring (scene references, prefab references). Mitigation: label inferred runtime wiring as inferred; ground everything else in code.
- **Risk:** The codebase is large; the document must be bounded to remain useful. Mitigation: depth-first coverage of the major subsystems, referencing file paths for further exploration.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Observed code-quality issues (god-class, hard-coded keys, duplicated coroutines, no tests, no CI) should be recorded in the document's observations section and as separate work items where warranted, not fixed as part of this task.
- **Environment risk:** `wl sync` failed on delete due to git worktree/LFS limitations in this environment; the analysis itself is not affected, but sync should be retried before finishing.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the architectural documentation live?" — Answer (operator): no explicit instruction given; reasonable assumption adopted: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` at repo root (matches the `docs/` convention referenced in AGENTS.md). Recorded as an assumption above; open to change.
- Q: "What scope does 'complete architectural analysis' cover?" — Answer (operator): no explicit instruction given; adopted scope: all first-party code under `Assets/_Rogue Wave` and `Assets/Wizards Code` (Game State, Story Teller, Command Terminal) plus documented roles of third-party frameworks (NeoFPS, Ink, Steamworks.NET, Feel, Discord). Recorded as an assumption above; open to change.
- Q: "Should the analysis also propose a target-state architecture (recommendations for refactoring)?" — Answer (operator, confirmed 2026-08-01): **Yes, make recommendations as notes.** The document will include an observations/risks section with maintainability concerns **and recommendations as notes** (no detailed target-state design, to keep the task bounded).

# Push to dev blocked: large binaries (Inky.exe 169MB) in Story Teller commits

## Problem statement

Push to `dev` on GitHub is rejected by the pre-receive hook (GH001) because the unpushed commits contain files larger than GitHub's 100MB limit. The blocker is the vendored Inky editor (`Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/`, ~516MB) added in commit `ba61d626` ("Story Teller ported to this project"), including `Inky.exe` (169MB), `inklecate_linux`/`inklecate_win.exe` (61MB/56MB, two copies each inside the app bundle), `app.asar` (24MB) and assorted Electron runtime binaries. `dev` is 21 commits ahead of `origin/dev`, all unpushed. Because `origin/dev` is an ancestor of local `dev`, the fix is a clean history rewrite of only the unpushed commits — no force-push is required.

## Users

- **The developer (primary):** cannot push `dev` at all, so work is not backed up and the release process (`dev` → `main`) is blocked.
- **Story authors:** use the Inky editor locally to write Ink scripts; they can install it from the upstream [Inky releases](https://github.com/inkle/inky) page instead of having it vendored in the repo.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want to `git push origin dev` successfully, so my work is backed up and the release pipeline is unblocked.
- As a story author, I want a documented way to get the Inky editor (link to upstream releases), so I can author Ink stories without the editor being committed to the repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The vendored Inky editor path `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` is removed from all 21 unpushed commits; after the rewrite, `git rev-list --objects origin/dev..dev` contains **no blob > 100MB** (and no `Inky/` files).
- `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` is added to `.gitignore` (after the `!Assets/Wizards Code` unignore at line 20) so the folder stays on disk for authoring but is never tracked again — verified with `git check-ignore`.
- `git push origin dev` succeeds as a **fast-forward** (no `--force`) — verified by an actual push; this is the definitive test since GitHub's pre-receive hook does not run on `--dry-run`.
- `origin/dev` and all other pushed refs are untouched: tip hash of `origin/dev` (`11af7ef9`) unchanged; `git log origin/dev..dev` shows the same logical changes minus the removed folder.
- The Inky editor remains on the local disk (untracked) — nothing is deleted from the working tree.
- `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/README.md` is updated: the vendored editor reference is replaced with a link to the upstream Inky releases; no other docs reference the vendored path.
- Post-rewrite repository is healthy: `git fsck` clean and no large blobs remain referenced in the rewritten range.

## Constraints

- **Never rewrite pushed history** (`origin/dev`, `origin/main`, remote tags). Only the 21 unpushed commits (`origin/dev..dev`) may be rewritten; no force-push.
- Keep the Inky editor **locally** (operator decision) — the rewrite removes it from git only.
- Leave other large-but-under-limit files in the range untouched (operator decision): `Reaper/Media/Ambient Sea Scape-003.wav` (68MB), `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Resources/Audio/Music/Ambient Sea - Reconstruction.wav` (39MB).
- `.gitignore` pattern order matters: the new ignore rule must come **after** the `!Assets/Wizards Code` unignore (line 20) to take effect.
- The working tree currently has uncommitted changes (including `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/...` files); commit or stash them before the history rewrite.
- `git filter-repo` is not installed; use `git filter-branch` (approach verified in a scratch repo: `git filter-branch -f --index-filter "git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch '<path>'" --prune-empty origin/dev..dev` preserves the merge topology, updates only `dev`, and prunes commits that become empty) or install filter-repo.
- The Ink runtime (`ink-unity-integration`, 3.6MB) is already a **git submodule** at `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/ink-unity-integration` — it must remain untouched.

## Existing state

- `dev` is 21 commits ahead of `origin/dev` (tip `11af7ef9` "Create issue templates"); the merge commit `0bf61611` already merged `origin/dev` into `dev`, so `origin/dev` is an ancestor — a fast-forward push is possible after the rewrite.
- Commit `ba61d626` added the vendored Inky editor; other large files in the range (`Reaper/Media/Ambient Sea Scape-003.wav`, the 39MB reconstruction wav) were added in `4e32d5fb` and later commits.
- The Story Teller README describes Inky as "a Windows editor for Ink files"; no runtime/build code references the Inky path — it is authoring-only.
- `.gitattributes` maps only GIFs and HDRI to LFS; the Inky binaries are plain blobs.
- `.git` is ~14GB; the largest blobs repo-wide are `Video/Raw` (1.2–3.6GB), reachable only from local-only tag `Release_2024.09.10.5237` (never pushed) — out of scope here, tracked as a follow-up.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the 21 unpushed commits to remove `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` from history (e.g. `git filter-branch` on the `origin/dev..dev` range; approach validated in a scratch repo).
2. Add a `.gitignore` entry for `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` after the `!Assets/Wizards Code` unignore.
3. Update `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/README.md` to point story authors at upstream Inky releases.
4. Commit the `.gitignore`/README changes, verify no >100MB blobs remain in the range, and push `origin dev` as a fast-forward.
5. The local Inky folder remains on disk, now untracked and ignored.

## Key Files

- `.gitignore` — add `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` after the `!Assets/Wizards Code` unignore (line 20).
- `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/README.md` — replace vendored-editor reference with link to upstream Inky releases.
- Git history on `dev` (commits `origin/dev..dev`) — rewrite to remove `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` (no working-tree file changes).

## Related work

- `RW-0MS9G83FW00295E5` — "Complete architectural analysis of the Rogue Wave codebase" (completed / in_review). This item was discovered during that work; its ARCHITECTURE.md commit is the 21st (docs-only) commit in the push range.
- `RW-0MSCDBAJ7006CMR8` — "Repo size hygiene: audit and LFS-migrate large binaries already in git history" (follow-up, created from this intake; `discovered-from:RW-0MSAC1OT80007AS4`).
- `RW-0MSCDBAJM003K3RT` — "Reaper/Media source-file tracking policy" (follow-up, created from this intake; `discovered-from:RW-0MSAC1OT80007AS4`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **History-rewrite scope risk:** rewriting only the unpushed range is safe, but a slip could touch pushed commits. Mitigation: target the exact range, verify `origin/dev` tip hash is unchanged before and after, and push without `--force` so GitHub refuses anything unexpected.
- **Uncommitted working-tree changes:** the tree is dirty; the rewrite requires a clean/stashed index — handle first.
- **Filter-branch prunes empty commits:** commits that only touched the Inky folder will disappear (acceptable — they were never pushed).
- **GitHub hook not dry-run testable:** `git push --dry-run` does not trigger the server pre-receive hook; the only definitive verification is a real push (acceptable risk, verified locally beforehand).
- **Assumption:** CI/build does not require the Inky editor (Unity project; Inky is an authoring tool, and the Ink runtime is already a submodule). No CI config references Inky.
- **Scope-creep risk:** other large files in the range (68MB/39MB wavs) stay as-is per operator decision; broader repo-size hygiene is tracked as follow-ups (`RW-0MSCDBAJ7006CMR8`, `RW-0MSCDBAJM003K3RT`) rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How to resolve the vendored Inky editor (the actual blocker)? a) Remove it via history rewrite + README link to upstream releases (recommended); b) Git LFS migrate; c) Submodule; d) Other." — Answer (operator): **"1. remove it from git, add to .gitignore"** — i.e. remove the Inky folder from git history, keep it on disk, and add it to `.gitignore`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "The non-blocking large files in the same commits (Reaper/Media/Ambient Sea Scape-003.wav 68MB, Ambient Sea - Reconstruction.wav 39MB): a) Leave as-is (recommended); b) Also migrate to LFS; c) Untrack the Reaper/Media wav." — Answer (operator): **"2. a"** — leave them as-is. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Scope: keep this work item strictly to unblocking the push, and file separate follow-up work items for broader repo-size hygiene? Or expand this item?" — Answer (operator): **"3. stay focused, create follow ups"** — keep this item focused on the push blocker; follow-ups created (`RW-0MSCDBAJ7006CMR8`, `RW-0MSCDBAJM003K3RT`). Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **RW-0MSCDBAJ7006CMR8** – Repo size hygiene: audit and LFS-migrate large binaries already in git history (open)
- **RW-0MSAD75MG007VKQP** – Data-model hygiene: encapsulate collections, custom serializer, centralized dirty-flagging (§8.8) (blocked) — keyword-match artifact; not directly related
- **RW-0MSCDBAJM003K3RT** – Reaper/Media source-file tracking policy (rpp/wav renders and backups) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` — keyword overlap only; no direct relevance to this item
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — keyword overlap only (agent-framework docs)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — keyword overlap only (agent-framework tooling)
data.title: Push to dev blocked: large binaries (Inky.exe 169MB) in Story Teller commits

# Refactoring Epic — Rogue Wave codebase

Consolidates the refactor recommendations from §8 "Observations, Risks & Recommendations" of **docs/ARCHITECTURE.md** (delivered in RW-0MS9G83FW00295E5, commit 52361f12).

The architectural analysis identified twelve observations; this epic tracks the actionable refactoring recommendations (§8.1–8.11; §8.12 is environment/build notes only and is not actionable here).

## Scope summary

- **High priority (foundational):** first-party unit test coverage (8.4) — explicitly flagged in the analysis as the prerequisite that makes the refactoring work safe; CI (8.5) to enforce it; split the RogueWaveGameMode god-class (8.1); deduplicate victory coroutines (8.2).
- **Medium priority:** centralize hard-coded stat keys (8.3), replace singleton discovery (8.6), data-model hygiene (8.8), deduplicate recipe logic across managers (8.10).
- **Low priority (polish/optimization):** performance improvements (8.7), dead-code removal (8.9), scene-wiring validation (8.11).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each recommendation has a child work item with a clear description and testable ACs
- [ ] Priorities assigned high → low reflecting the analysis's risk ordering (tests/CI first)
- [ ] Dependency edges recorded with `wl dep` — behavior-changing refactors depend on test coverage (8.4)
- [ ] Children completed in dependency order; epic only closed after all children are closed

## References

- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8 (source of all recommendations)
- RW-0MS9G83FW00295E5 (delivery work item)
data.title: Refactoring recommendations from architectural analysis (§8 of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

data.description:
Add a Unity Test Framework (EditMode) test assembly covering pure game logic identified in the architectural analysis as untested:

- RogueLitePersistentData.Add / RogueLiteRunData.Add — recipe stacking, max-stack enforcement, weapon build-order insertion
- RecipeManager.GetOffers / GetOfferCandidates — weighted-random offer generation
- WeightedRandom<T> — weighted selection
- WfcDefinition.challengeRating / Duration computation
- LevelGenerator.isValidateLevel — level validation (spawn point present, no fully enclosed interiors)

Source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.4 (No first-party unit tests). This is the foundational item — the analysis explicitly states refactoring (8.1, 8.2, 8.10, etc.) is risky without this coverage, and other items depend on it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New test assembly (asmdef) exists under a first-party Tests/ directory, excluded from builds
- [ ] Tests cover at minimum: recipe stacking & build-order logic, offer generation, WeightedRandom, challenge rating, level validation
- [ ] All tests pass in Unity EditMode
- [ ] Tests are runnable from CI (see §8.5 work item)
data.title: Add first-party unit test coverage for pure game logic (§8.4)

data.description:
RogueWaveGameMode (Assets/_Rogue Wave/Runtime/Game Management/RogueWaveGameMode.cs, 992 lines) is the central orchestrator handling spawning, loadout configuration, victory/death/extraction coroutines, stats logging, HUD updates, spawner/portal/enemy registration, save triggers, and campaign access. It reaches into LevelGenerator, AIDirector, NanobotManager, GameStatsManager, MusicManager, AudioManager, RogueLiteManager, MovementUpgradeManager, and UI controllers.

Recommended split (from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.1):
- RunFlowController — victory/death state machine
- LoadoutController — build loadout from RunData
- LevelDirector — spawner/portal/enemy registration
- StatsReporter — game-log/stat wiring

Keep RogueWaveGameMode as a thin composition root.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RogueWaveGameMode no longer exceeds ~300 lines and delegates to the new collaborators
- [ ] No behaviour change: existing scenes/prefabs work without re-wiring (or wiring changes documented)
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests added for extracted collaborators where behaviour is non-trivial
- [ ] Each collaborator has a single clear responsibility

DEPENDS ON: unit test coverage (8.4) — refactoring without regression protection is explicitly flagged as risky in the analysis.
data.title: Split RogueWaveGameMode god-class into focused collaborators (§8.1)

data.description:
RogueWaveGameMode contains three near-identical victory coroutines: DelayedLevelTimerAchievedCoroutine, DelayedLevelClearedCoroutine, and DelayedLevelCompleteCoroutine. They share extraction FX, magnet buff, currentGameLevel++, victory stat, and victory action logic.

Recommendation (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.2): extract a single LevelCompletedCoroutine(extractionType, victoryAction) parameterized by extraction type, so bug fixes (e.g. the magnet restore) apply consistently across all victory paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One parameterized level-completion coroutine replaces the three duplicated implementations
- [ ] Behaviour identical across all three victory paths (timer, boss-spawners-cleared, portal)
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover each victory path where feasible
- [ ] No dead code left behind (see also §8.9)

DEPENDS ON: unit test coverage (8.4).
data.title: Deduplicate victory coroutines into single parameterized flow (§8.2)

data.description:
No .github/workflows exist — there is no automated build, test, or validation on commit. Regressions ship silently; the README's documented 'revert after asset import' workflow is manual.

Recommendation (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.5): add a CI workflow running Unity in batch mode:
- Compile check (both platforms)
- Run EditMode tests (needs §8.4 test coverage)
- Run recipe/level data validation (DataValidation.ValidateRecipes)
- Optional: smoke-play via a dev scene

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] .github/workflows/ contains a Unity CI workflow
- [ ] CI runs on push/PR to dev
- [ ] Compile check + EditMode tests + data validation execute in batch mode
- [ ] CI status is visible on the repo (badge or status checks)

DEPENDS ON: unit test coverage (8.4) — CI is most valuable once tests exist.
data.title: Add CI pipeline (Unity batch mode: compile, tests, data validation) (§8.5)

data.description:
Managers are discovered via FindObjectOfType/FindFirstObjectByType in Instance getters (GameStatsManager, AIDirector, StoryManager, MusicManager) with auto-creation fallbacks; RogueWaveGameMode lazily caches FindObjectOfType<CampaignManager>(), FindAnyObjectByType<AIDirector>(), FindObjectOfType<HudGameStatusController>().

Risks (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.6): hidden scene dependencies; multiple managers in a scene lead to non-deterministic duplicate destruction; auto-created instances may lack serialized config.

Recommendation: prefer explicit scene references / service registration; validate singleton presence in scene at editor time (extend DataValidation).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All manager discovery via FindObjectOfType* in Instance getters / game mode replaced with explicit references or a service-registration pattern
- [ ] Editor-time validation confirms required singletons exist in each scene (extend DataValidation)
- [ ] No runtime behaviour change; scenes without required managers fail fast with clear errors
- [ ] All existing tests pass

DEPENDS ON: unit test coverage (8.4).
data.title: Replace FindObjectOfType singleton discovery with explicit references (§8.6)

data.description:
Stat keys are string literals throughout the codebase: "RESOURCES" (RogueWaveGameMode.cs, NanobotManager.cs, RecipeManager.cs, ResourceCommands.cs, HubController.cs), "TOTAL_TIME_IN_RUNS", "RUNS_STARTED", "RUNS_COMPLETED", "DEATH_COUNT", "MAX_NANOBOT_LEVEL", "RESOURCES_SPENT_IN_RUNS", "RUN_LOG" (GameStatsManager.GetDataAsYAML). Code contains TODO: Remove hard coding of resource stat key comments.

Risks (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.3): typos silently create null stats; renaming a stat asset breaks logic without a compile error.

Recommendation: centralize stat keys in a constants class or a stat-key ScriptableObject catalog; add editor validation for key references.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All stat-key string literals replaced by references to a central constants class or catalog
- [ ] No runtime behaviour change
- [ ] Editor validation flags unknown/misspelled stat keys (extend DataValidation)
- [ ] All existing tests pass; tests updated where stat keys were asserted

DEPENDS ON: unit test coverage (8.4).
data.title: Centralize hard-coded stat keys (§8.3)

data.description:
Recipe add/stack logic and weapon-build-order insertion are duplicated between RogueLitePersistentData.Add and RogueLiteRunData.Add (code contains an explicit 'REFACTOR: this code is a duplicate of code in the persistent data class' comment). NanobotManager.AddToRunRecipes uses a long if/else dispatch (with its own TODO: This is messy comment) rather than polymorphism on AbstractRecipe.

Recommendation (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.10): move stacking/build-order rules into a single RecipeCollection type; dispatch via virtual methods on AbstractRecipe (e.g. OnAddedToRun(NanobotManager)).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single RecipeCollection type used by both persistent and run data
- [ ] NanobotManager.AddToRunRecipes dispatch replaced with polymorphic hooks on AbstractRecipe

**Problem:** The local .git pack is ~14GB. Several large binary blobs exist in already-committed history and are not stored in Git LFS, bloating clones and risking future push rejections.

**Findings (from intake of RW-0MSAC1OT80007AS4):**
- `Video/Raw/*` blobs of 1.2–3.6GB (≈9.7GB total) are reachable only from local tag `Release_2024.09.10.5237` — this tag does not appear in `git ls-remote --tags origin`, so these were likely never pushed; they are dead weight that can be dropped and garbage-collected.
- `GIFs/Nanobot *` (97MB, 96MB) and `GIFs/Radar *` (66MB) exist as real blobs in history despite `*.gif` being LFS-tracked in .gitattributes (committed before LFS was enabled).
- `Reaper/Media/Streamer 101 *` wavs (78MB × 2), `Assets/_Marketing/Scenes/Technology is Magic/ReflectionProbe-1.exr` (79MB), `Reaper/Media/Ambient Sea Scape-003.wav` (68MB), `Assets/_Rogue Wave/Resources/Audio/Music/Ambient Sea - Reconstruction.wav` (41MB) are tracked as plain blobs.
- HDRI (.hdr) files are already LFS pointers — the LFS setup pattern exists and can be reused.

**User story:** As a developer, I want the repository to stay small and pushable, so that clones are fast and future pushes are never blocked by the 100MB GitHub limit.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An audit report lists all blobs >25MB, their size, reachability (branches/tags/remotes), and LFS status.
- Decided outcome per file (migrate to LFS vs. remove vs. keep) is documented on this item.
- Large blobs retained are stored via Git LFS (pointer in history) OR intentionally kept as plain blobs with justification.
- Dead blobs (e.g. Video/Raw reachable only from local-only tag) are removed and `git gc` reduces pack size; clone size measurably reduced.
- No pushed history is rewritten without explicit operator approval (force-push/rewrite of origin refs requires sign-off).

# Add Inky to .gitignore and update Story Teller README

## Summary
Prepare the repo so the vendored Inky editor is never tracked again and story authors are directed to upstream releases, then commit the working-tree changes so the history rewrite runs from a clean index.

Parent: RW-0MSAC1OT80007AS4 (Push to dev blocked: large binaries in Story Teller commits)

## User story
As a story author, I want a documented way to get the Inky editor (link to upstream releases), so I can author Ink stories without the editor being committed to the repo.

## Implementation
1. Add `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` to `.gitignore` AFTER the `!Assets/Wizards Code` unignore (currently line 20) — pattern order matters for it to take effect.
2. Update `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/README.md`: replace the vendored-editor reference ("[Inky](https://github.com/inkle/inky) - a Windows editor for Ink files") with a link to upstream Inky releases (https://github.com/inkle/inky/releases). Note the README currently has a large uncommitted diff (likely line-ending/whitespace) — preserve intent, change only the Inky reference.
3. Verify no other docs reference the vendored Inky path (grep for "Story Teller/Inky").
4. Commit the .gitignore + README changes together with the other uncommitted working-tree changes (or stash them) so the tree/index is clean for the history rewrite in the sibling task. The Inky folder stays on disk, untracked and ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `git check-ignore "Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/Inky.exe"` returns the path (exit 0), proving the ignore rule works.
- The ignore rule appears after the `!Assets/Wizards Code` unignore in `.gitignore`.
- `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/README.md` links to upstream Inky releases and no longer describes Inky as a vendored editor component.
- No other tracked docs reference `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky`.
- The working tree/index is clean (uncommitted changes committed or stashed) and the Inky folder is untracked.
- No `Inky/` files are included in the new commit (verified by `git show --stat`).

## Constraints
- Keep the Inky editor locally on disk — remove from git tracking only.
- Do not rewrite history in this task (sibling task does that).
- Match existing .gitignore style; minimal, surgical edits.

## Key files
- .gitignore
- Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/README.md

# Rewrite unpushed history to remove vendored Inky editor

## Summary
Use `git filter-branch` over the unpushed range (`origin/dev..dev`, 21+ commits) to strip `Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky/` from every commit, pruning commits that become empty, without touching any pushed history.

Parent: RW-0MSAC1OT80007AS4 (Push to dev blocked: large binaries in Story Teller commits)

## User story
As a developer, I want the vendored Inky editor removed from unpushed history, so the push to dev is no longer rejected by GitHub's 100MB pre-receive hook.

## Implementation
1. Confirm working tree is clean (sibling task committed/stashed changes). If not, stop and surface.
2. Record baseline: `git rev-parse origin/dev` must be `11af7ef945bf0e2bf31022ff9934fceded08041b`; `git rev-list --count origin/dev..dev` (expect 21 before the new commit, 22 after sibling commit).
3. Run the validated approach:
   `git filter-branch -f --index-filter "git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch 'Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/Inky'" --prune-empty origin/dev..dev`
   This preserves merge topology, updates only `dev`, and prunes commits that become empty (acceptable — never pushed).
4. Note: commits that only touched Inky will be pruned; the ARCHITECTURE.md docs commit should survive.
5. Do NOT delete the on-disk Inky folder — it must remain for authoring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `git rev-parse origin/dev` still equals `11af7ef945bf0e2bf31022ff9934fceded08041b` (pushed history untouched).
- `git rev-list --objects origin/dev..dev | grep Inky` returns no `Inky/` files.
- No blob > 100MB remains in the range (`git rev-list --objects origin/dev..dev | git cat-file --batch-check` filter).
- `git log origin/dev..dev` shows the same logical changes minus the removed folder (docs commit, tutorial commits, etc. still present).
- The `ink-unity-integration` submodule entry (`Assets/Wizards Code/Story Teller/ink-unity-integration`) is untouched.
- The Inky folder remains on local disk (untracked).
- `git status` shows no unexpected changes after the rewrite.

## Constraints
- NEVER rewrite pushed history: only `origin/dev..dev` range; no force-push in this task.
- Leave Reaper/Media wav (68MB) and 39MB reconstruction wav untouched (operator decision).
- Keep the Inky editor locally (operator decision).
- Use filter-branch (filter-repo not installed) or install filter-repo if problems arise.

## Key files
- Git history on dev (commits origin/dev..dev)

# Verify rewritten history and fast-forward push dev

## Summary
Run post-rewrite integrity checks (fsck, large-blob scan, log comparison), then push `dev` to `origin` as a fast-forward (no --force) and confirm the push is accepted — the definitive test since GitHub's pre-receive hook does not run on --dry-run.

Parent: RW-0MSAC1OT80007AS4 (Push to dev blocked: large binaries in Story Teller commits)

## User story
As a developer, I want `git push origin dev` to succeed, so my work is backed up and the release pipeline is unblocked.

## Implementation
1. Verify repository health: `git fsck --full` clean; no dangling large blobs from the rewritten range.
2. Confirm no blob > 100MB in range: `git rev-list --objects origin/dev..dev | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$1=="blob" && $3>104857600'` returns nothing.
3. Confirm `origin/dev` tip hash unchanged (11af7ef945bf0e2bf31022ff9934fceded08041b).
4. Sanity-compare logical changes: `git log --oneline origin/dev..dev` — same changes minus removed folder.
5. Verify fast-forward possible: `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/dev dev` exit 0.
6. Push: `git push origin dev` WITHOUT --force. If rejected, stop and investigate (do not force).
7. Confirm push succeeded: `git rev-parse origin/dev` equals local `dev` tip; remote output shows fast-forward.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `git fsck --full` reports no errors.
- No blob > 100MB in `origin/dev..dev`.
- `git push origin dev` succeeds as a fast-forward with no --force flag.
- `origin/dev` now equals the local `dev` tip hash.
- No other refs (main, tags) were pushed or modified.
- The 68MB/39MB wav files remain in the range (untouched per operator decision).

## Constraints
- Never use --force; the push must be a clean fast-forward.
- Do not push to main.
- If the push is rejected for any reason, stop and report — do not work around the hook.

## Key files
- Remote refs origin/dev, origin/main (read-only)
